summary_en: Accenture Japan Ltd. launched a tender offer for all outstanding ordinary shares of Global Security Experts Inc. at 8,500 yen per share and warrants at 1 yen each, with a minimum acceptance threshold of 983,100 shares (66.37% post-acquisition) over a 30-business-day period from November 2 to December 15, 2026, to take the company private. The board unanimously endorsed the offer and recommended shareholders to tender their shares.
title_en: Notice of Expression of Support and Recommendation to Tender with Respect to Tender Offer for Our Shares and Other Securities by Accenture Japan Ltd.
translation_en_brief:
Accenture Japan Ltd., a wholly-owned subsidiary of Accenture plc listed on the New York Stock Exchange, launched a tender offer to acquire all outstanding ordinary shares and warrants of Global Security Experts Inc. on October 30, 2026. The offer price was set at 8,500 yen per ordinary share and 1 yen per warrant. The minimum threshold for acceptance was 983,100 shares, representing a 66.37% post-acquisition ownership stake, calculated using the total voting rights as of March 31, 2026 (151,651 units) disclosed in the company's 43rd fiscal year securities report filed on June 24, 2026. The tender offer was scheduled to run for 30 business days from November 2 to December 15, 2026. The stated purpose was to take Global Security Experts Inc. private through a series of procedures following the tender offer, leading to the delisting of its shares from the Tokyo Stock Exchange Growth Market.

The board of Global Security Experts Inc. held a meeting on the announcement date and formally expressed support for the tender offer. The board recommended all shareholders to tender their shares in the offer. For holders of warrants issued pursuant to a February 22, 2021 board resolution (exercisable from February 23, 2023 to February 22, 2031), the board left the decision to participate in the tender offer to the warrant holders' discretion. At the time of announcement, Global Security Experts Inc. and Accenture Japan Ltd. had no capital or human relations, though they maintained a subcontracting business relationship. The board's resolution was taken with the condition and premise that Accenture Japan Ltd. intended to make Global Security Experts Inc. a wholly-owned subsidiary and that the delisting of the company's shares was planned.
